title: Founding of the Lan Xang Kingdom
description: Fa Ngum united Lao principalities to found Lan Xang, the 'Land of a Million Elephants', the first unified Lao kingdom.

title: Vientiane Becomes Capital
description: King Setthathirath moved the Lan Xang capital to Vientiane and built the That Luang stupa, a national symbol of Laos.

title: Division of Lan Xang
description: The kingdom fragmented into the rival realms of Luang Prabang, Vientiane, and later Champasak.

title: French Protectorate Established
description: Following the Franco-Siamese War, Laos became a French protectorate within French Indochina.

title: Independence from France
description: Laos gained full independence from France, becoming the Kingdom of Laos under King Sisavang Vong.

title: Lao People's Democratic Republic Founded
description: The Pathet Lao abolished the monarchy and established a communist state, the Lao People's Democratic Republic.

title: Laos Joins ASEAN
description: Laos became a member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, deepening regional integration.

title: Founding of the Malacca Sultanate
description: Parameswara founded Malacca, which became a powerful trading port and center for the spread of Islam in the region.

title: Portuguese Capture of Malacca
description: Portuguese forces under Afonso de Albuquerque conquered Malacca, beginning European colonial influence in the area.

title: Dutch Capture of Malacca
description: The Dutch East India Company seized Malacca from the Portuguese, controlling the vital strait's trade.

title: British Settlement of Penang
description: Francis Light established a British trading post on Penang, expanding British presence on the Malay Peninsula.

title: Independence of Malaya
description: The Federation of Malaya gained independence from Britain, with Tunku Abdul Rahman as its first prime minister.

title: Formation of Malaysia
description: Malaya, Singapore, Sabah, and Sarawak merged to form Malaysia, though Singapore left two years later.

title: Petronas Towers Completed
description: Kuala Lumpur's Petronas Twin Towers became the world's tallest buildings, symbolizing Malaysia's rapid development.

title: Conversion to Islam
description: The Maldives converted to Islam, traditionally credited to a visiting scholar, ending the earlier Buddhist era.

title: Portuguese Occupation
description: The Portuguese briefly occupied the Maldives until Muhammad Thakurufaanu led a successful rebellion in 1573.

title: British Protectorate
description: The Maldives became a British protectorate, retaining internal self-rule while Britain managed defense and foreign affairs.

title: Independence from Britain
description: The Maldives gained full independence from the United Kingdom and later joined the United Nations.

title: Republic Declared
description: Following a referendum, the sultanate was abolished and the Maldives became a republic.

title: Indian Ocean Tsunami
description: The devastating tsunami struck the low-lying Maldives, highlighting the nation's vulnerability to rising seas.

title: First Multiparty Election
description: Mohamed Nasheed won the Maldives' first multiparty presidential election, ending decades of single-party rule.

title: Rise of the Xiongnu Confederation
description: Modu Chanyu unified nomadic tribes of the Mongolian steppe into the powerful Xiongnu confederation.

title: Genghis Khan Unites the Mongols
description: Temujin was proclaimed Genghis Khan, founding the Mongol Empire that would become history's largest contiguous empire.

title: Kublai Khan Founds the Yuan Dynasty
description: Genghis Khan's grandson Kublai established the Yuan dynasty, ruling China as part of the Mongol realm.

title: Adoption of Tibetan Buddhism
description: Altan Khan granted the title 'Dalai Lama', cementing Tibetan Buddhism as the dominant Mongolian faith.

title: Declaration of Independence from Qing
description: Outer Mongolia declared independence from the collapsing Qing dynasty under the Bogd Khan.

title: Mongolian People's Republic
description: Mongolia became a communist state, the world's second, closely aligned with the Soviet Union.

title: Democratic Revolution
description: Peaceful protests ended one-party rule, leading Mongolia to adopt multiparty democracy and a market economy.

title: Founding of the Pagan Kingdom
description: King Anawrahta unified Myanmar under the Pagan Empire and promoted Theravada Buddhism across the land.

title: Spread of Theravada Buddhism
description: Anawrahta's conquest of Thaton brought Buddhist scriptures to Pagan, shaping Burmese religious culture for centuries.

title: Founding of the Konbaung Dynasty
description: Alaungpaya founded the Konbaung dynasty, the last Burmese royal dynasty, reunifying the country.

title: British Annexation of Burma
description: After the Third Anglo-Burmese War, Britain annexed all of Burma, ending the monarchy and exiling King Thibaw.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Burma gained independence from the United Kingdom, becoming a sovereign republic outside the Commonwealth.

title: Military Coup
description: General Ne Win seized power, beginning decades of military-dominated socialist rule in Burma.

title: Aung San Suu Kyi Nobel Peace Prize
description: Pro-democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi won the Nobel Peace Prize while under house arrest.

title: Birth of the Buddha at Lumbini
description: Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, was traditionally born at Lumbini in present-day Nepal, founding Buddhism.

title: Licchavi Dynasty Inscriptions
description: The Licchavi kingdom flourished in the Kathmandu Valley, leaving Nepal's earliest dated inscriptions under Manadeva.

title: Unification of Nepal
description: Prithvi Narayan Shah conquered the Kathmandu Valley, unifying the modern state of Nepal under the Shah dynasty.

title: Treaty of Sugauli
description: After the Anglo-Nepalese War, Nepal ceded territory to Britain but retained independence, defining its borders.

title: End of Rana Rule
description: A revolution ended the century-long autocratic Rana regime and restored power to the Shah monarchy.

title: First Ascent of Mount Everest
description: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary reached the summit of Everest, the world's highest peak on Nepal's border.

title: Abolition of the Monarchy
description: Nepal's constituent assembly abolished the 240-year-old monarchy and declared a federal democratic republic.

title: Legendary Founding of Gojoseon
description: Korean tradition dates the founding of Gojoseon, the first Korean kingdom, by Dangun on the peninsula.

title: Founding of Goguryeo
description: The kingdom of Goguryeo arose in the north, centered on territory that includes present-day North Korea.

title: Japanese Annexation of Korea
description: Japan annexed the entire Korean Peninsula, beginning 35 years of colonial rule over the future North Korea.

title: Founding of North Korea
description: The Democratic People's Republic of Korea was established under Kim Il-sung following the peninsula's division.

title: Outbreak of the Korean War
description: North Korean forces invaded the South, triggering the Korean War that devastated the peninsula until 1953.

title: Korean Armistice Agreement
description: An armistice halted the Korean War, establishing the Demilitarized Zone but leaving the two Koreas technically at war.

title: First Nuclear Test
description: North Korea conducted its first underground nuclear weapons test, drawing international sanctions.

title: Indus Valley Civilization at Mohenjo-daro
description: The advanced urban Indus Valley Civilization flourished at sites like Mohenjo-daro and Harappa in present-day Pakistan.

title: Achaemenid Conquest of Gandhara
description: Darius I incorporated Gandhara and the Indus region into the Persian Achaemenid Empire.

title: Alexander Reaches the Indus
description: Alexander the Great fought King Porus at the Hydaspes River, bringing Greek influence to the region.

title: Arab Conquest of Sindh
description: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh, introducing Islam to the Indus region and shaping its religious future.

title: Independence and Partition
description: Pakistan was created as a homeland for South Asian Muslims when British India was partitioned, led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

title: Independence of Bangladesh
description: East Pakistan seceded after civil war to become Bangladesh, splitting the country in two.

title: Nuclear Weapons Tests
description: Pakistan conducted its first nuclear tests in response to India's, becoming a declared nuclear power.

title: Laguna Copperplate Inscription
description: The earliest known Philippine document records a debt settlement, showing early literacy and Indianized trade links.

title: Arrival of Ferdinand Magellan
description: Magellan reached the islands during his circumnavigation; he was killed by Lapulapu at the Battle of Mactan.

title: Spanish Colonization Begins
description: Miguel López de Legazpi established the first permanent Spanish settlement, starting over three centuries of colonial rule.

title: Declaration of Independence from Spain
description: Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence, though the U.S. soon took control after the Spanish-American War.

title: Independence from the United States
description: The Philippines gained full sovereignty from the United States, becoming an independent republic.

title: Marcos Era Begins
description: Ferdinand Marcos was elected president and later declared martial law, ruling for over two decades.

title: People Power Revolution
description: Peaceful EDSA protests ousted Marcos and restored democracy under Corazon Aquino.

title: Founding of Modern Singapore
description: Stamford Raffles established a British trading post on Singapore, transforming it into a key commercial port.

title: Singapore Becomes a Crown Colony
description: The Straits Settlements, including Singapore, came under direct British colonial administration.

title: Fall of Singapore
description: Japanese forces captured Singapore during World War II, beginning a harsh occupation until 1945.

title: Self-Government Achieved
description: Singapore gained internal self-government from Britain, with Lee Kuan Yew becoming its first prime minister.

title: Merger with Malaysia
description: Singapore joined the Federation of Malaysia, ending British colonial rule.

title: Independence as a Republic
description: Singapore separated from Malaysia to become an independent sovereign nation under Lee Kuan Yew.

title: Goh Chok Tong Succeeds Lee Kuan Yew
description: Lee Kuan Yew stepped down after 31 years, marking a peaceful leadership transition for the prosperous city-state.

title: Legendary Founding of Gojoseon
description: Korean tradition credits Dangun with founding Gojoseon, regarded as the first Korean kingdom.

title: Silla Unifies Korea
description: The kingdom of Silla, allied with Tang China, unified most of the Korean Peninsula for the first time.

title: Creation of Hangul
description: King Sejong the Great promulgated Hangul, the Korean alphabet, to promote widespread literacy.

title: Japanese Annexation of Korea
description: Japan formally annexed Korea, beginning 35 years of colonial rule that ended in 1945.

title: Founding of the Republic of Korea
description: South Korea was established as the Republic of Korea, with Syngman Rhee as its first president.

title: Seoul Summer Olympics
description: Seoul hosted the Summer Olympics, showcasing South Korea's rapid economic rise and democratization.

title: Korean War Armistice
description: An armistice ended active fighting in the Korean War, leaving South Korea divided from the North along the DMZ.

title: Founding of Anuradhapura Kingdom
description: The Anuradhapura Kingdom was established, becoming a long-lasting center of Sinhalese civilization and Buddhism.

title: Introduction of Buddhism
description: The monk Mahinda, son of Emperor Ashoka, introduced Buddhism to Sri Lanka, which became central to its culture.

title: Arrival of the Portuguese
description: Portuguese traders arrived and gradually established control over coastal Sri Lanka and its spice trade.

title: Fall of the Kingdom of Kandy
description: The British annexed the Kingdom of Kandy, bringing the entire island under colonial rule as Ceylon.

title: Independence as Ceylon
description: Ceylon gained independence from Britain, later renaming itself Sri Lanka in 1972.

title: World's First Female Prime Minister
description: Sirimavo Bandaranaike became the world's first elected female head of government.

title: End of the Civil War
description: The government defeated the Tamil Tigers, ending a devastating 26-year civil war.

title: Alexander Conquers Sogdiana
description: Alexander the Great campaigned through Sogdiana, in present-day Tajikistan, founding Hellenistic settlements.

title: Rise of the Samanid Dynasty
description: The Persian Samanid dynasty flourished, fostering a revival of Persian culture honored by Tajiks today.

title: Russian Conquest of Central Asia
description: The Russian Empire extended its control over the region that would become Tajikistan.

title: Tajik Soviet Republic Formed
description: Tajikistan became a full constituent republic of the Soviet Union, separate from Uzbekistan.

title: Independence from the Soviet Union
description: Tajikistan declared independence as the USSR collapsed, becoming a sovereign nation.

title: Outbreak of Civil War
description: A devastating civil war erupted shortly after independence, lasting until a peace accord in 1997.

title: Peace Accord Ends Civil War
description: A UN-brokered peace agreement ended the Tajik civil war, paving the way for national reconciliation.

title: Founding of the Sukhothai Kingdom
description: The Sukhothai Kingdom emerged as the first major Thai state, often seen as the cradle of Thai civilization.

title: Creation of the Thai Script
description: King Ramkhamhaeng is traditionally credited with creating the Thai alphabet at Sukhothai.

title: Founding of Ayutthaya
description: The Ayutthaya Kingdom was founded and grew into a powerful and prosperous Siamese empire.

title: Founding of the Chakri Dynasty
description: Rama I founded the Chakri dynasty and established Bangkok as the capital, which rules Thailand to this day.

title: Transition to Constitutional Monarchy
description: A bloodless revolution ended absolute monarchy, establishing a constitutional monarchy in Siam.

title: Renamed Thailand
description: Siam was officially renamed Thailand, meaning 'Land of the Free', reflecting national identity.

title: Reign of King Bhumibol Begins
description: Bhumibol Adulyadej ascended the throne and reigned for 70 years, the longest in Thai history.

title: Portuguese Arrival in Timor
description: Portuguese traders arrived in Timor seeking sandalwood, beginning centuries of colonial presence.

title: Establishment of Dili
description: The Portuguese established Dili as the colonial capital of Portuguese Timor.

title: Independence Declared and Invaded
description: Timor-Leste declared independence from Portugal, but Indonesia invaded and annexed the territory days later.

title: Santa Cruz Massacre
description: Indonesian forces killed protesters in Dili, drawing global attention to the East Timorese independence struggle.

title: Independence Referendum
description: East Timorese voted overwhelmingly for independence from Indonesia in a UN-supervised referendum.

title: Full Independence Restored
description: Timor-Leste became a fully independent nation, the first new sovereign state of the 21st century.

title: Nobel Peace Prize for Belo and Ramos-Horta
description: Bishop Belo and José Ramos-Horta won the Nobel Peace Prize for their work toward a just resolution in East Timor.

title: Achaemenid Rule over Margiana
description: The region of Margiana, around Merv, became part of the Persian Achaemenid Empire.

title: Merv Becomes Islamic Center
description: Arab conquest brought Islam to Merv, which grew into a major center of learning on the Silk Road.

title: Mongol Destruction of Merv
description: Genghis Khan's Mongol armies sacked Merv, then one of the world's largest cities.

title: Russian Conquest of Turkmen Lands
description: The Russian Empire defeated Turkmen tribes at Geok Tepe, incorporating the region into Russian Central Asia.

title: Turkmen Soviet Republic Formed
description: Turkmenistan was established as a constituent republic of the Soviet Union.

title: Independence from the Soviet Union
description: Turkmenistan declared independence as the USSR dissolved, with Saparmurat Niyazov becoming its leader.

title: Recognized as Neutral State
description: The United Nations recognized Turkmenistan's status of permanent neutrality.

title: Alexander Conquers Samarkand
description: Alexander the Great captured Samarkand (Maracanda), one of Central Asia's oldest continuously inhabited cities.

title: Battle of Talas
description: Arab and Tang Chinese forces clashed near the region, after which Islam and papermaking spread through Central Asia.

title: Timur Establishes His Empire
description: Timur (Tamerlane) made Samarkand the capital of a vast empire, sponsoring magnificent architecture and learning.

title: Ulugh Beg's Observatory
description: Timur's grandson Ulugh Beg built a great observatory in Samarkand, producing influential astronomical tables.

title: Russian Conquest of Tashkent
description: The Russian Empire captured Tashkent, extending its rule across the Uzbek lands.

title: Uzbek Soviet Republic Formed
description: Uzbekistan was created as a constituent republic of the Soviet Union.

title: Independence from the Soviet Union
description: Uzbekistan declared independence as the USSR collapsed, becoming a sovereign state under Islam Karimov.

title: Founding of Âu Lạc Kingdom
description: An Dương Vương founded the kingdom of Âu Lạc, building the fortified citadel of Cổ Loa in the Red River Delta.

title: Chinese Han Conquest
description: The Han dynasty conquered northern Vietnam, beginning roughly a thousand years of Chinese domination.

title: Battle of Bạch Đằng
description: Ngô Quyền defeated Chinese forces on the Bạch Đằng River, securing Vietnamese independence.

title: Founding of the Nguyễn Dynasty
description: Emperor Gia Long unified Vietnam and founded the Nguyễn dynasty, the country's last imperial dynasty.

title: Declaration of Independence
description: Hồ Chí Minh declared Vietnam's independence from France, founding the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

title: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
description: Vietnamese forces decisively defeated the French, ending colonial rule and dividing the country at the 17th parallel.

title: Fall of Saigon and Reunification
description: The Vietnam War ended with the fall of Saigon, leading to the reunification of Vietnam in 1976.
